# The command line

<!-- Generated by go run ./adapters/cli/gen from adapters/cli and adapters/errtext; do not edit. -->

Every command of `placket`: what it does, its usage, its arguments and flags, what its `--json` object follows, and the exit codes it ends with. A command prints prose for a person on standard error, and JSON or a body on standard output. A command that is refused or fails ends standard error with one line: `rejected <code>` when the window refused the call, `rejected founding <code>` when it refused an acceptance, `door <code>` when the window's door refused it, and `error <code>` for any other, with any detail after the code. [Errors](#errors) gives each code's cause and fix.

With `--json`, every command but `mcp` prints its result as one JSON object on standard output instead; its exit code and standard error stay the same. Each command's object holds the members [section 11 of the protocol](../../spec/protocol.md#11-what-the-command-line-prints-for-a-script) gives it, under the requirement ids each command below cites.

In a usage, `<socket flags>` stands for `--key <file> --socket <path> --accord <id>`, or `--label <label>` in their place, and then `[--state <dir>]`: the flags of every command that calls a window. A flag in square brackets is optional, `|` separates flags of which one is given, and `...` after a flag means it may be given more than once.

`placket <command> --help` prints a command's flags on standard output, each with the sentence this page gives it, and exits 0 ([commands-1](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-1-one-object-on-standard-output)).

## Exit codes

| Code | What it means |
|---|---|
| `0` | A pass, or a command that did what it was asked. |
| `1` | A block on `give`, `answer` or `change`; a release that blocked; a `give --wait` or `result` whose question closed any way but an accept that passed and was released; a comment that did not cross; a file, or a value inside it, that no release matches; a log that does not conform, or a body that is not its receipt's part, in `verify`. |
| `2` | A rejection: the window refused the call, and standard error ends `rejected` and its code. |
| `3` | A tool or door error: standard error ends `error`, or `door`, and its code. |
| `4` | An ask still open: the question's id is on standard output. |

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`init`](#init) | Found an example Accord for one person, who holds every key, and print what to run next. |
| [`key`](#key) | Make a key file, or print a key file's actor reference. |
| [`key new`](#key-new) | Write a new key file, mode 0600, and print its actor reference; it never prints the seed. |
| [`key ref`](#key-ref) | Print the actor reference of a key file. |
| [`declare`](#declare) | Sign the key's declaration of its terms and print it. |
| [`seal`](#seal) | Seal the key's own signed declaration: print the seal entry for founding, and write the opening for whoever runs the window. |
| [`bind`](#bind) | Sign, as a principal, a binding that gives an actor its roles under one mediator and one policy until a time, and print it. |
| [`founding`](#founding) | Put a policy, a mediator, a card, the seals and the bindings in one founding set, check that it founds, and print it with its Accord id and card hash. |
| [`card`](#card) | Print this build's card, with the judges' configs given, and its card hash and the module it names. |
| [`window`](#window) | Run the mediator of an Accord behind its door, on a unix socket, with its journal, until it is interrupted. |
| [`window close`](#window-close) | Close the Accord of a stopped window's journal: close each open question, write the close receipt last, and with `--socket` serve the closed Accord. |
| [`view`](#view) | Ask the window for the key's own view of a proposed Accord, keep it in the state directory, and print it. |
| [`accept`](#accept) | Sign the key's acceptance of the view its state directory keeps, hand it to the window, and say whether the Accord is now founded. |
| [`give`](#give) | Give another member one part, and print the outcome: pass, block, or ask, with the question's id. |
| [`questions`](#questions) | Print the open questions this key may answer, one JSON object per line. |
| [`watch`](#watch) | Wait on the questions of one or more mediators and print each new question once, as it opens, with the lines that answer it; it never answers. |
| [`answer`](#answer) | Accept a question, asking for release unless `--no-release`, and print the answer's outcome, then the release's. |
| [`change`](#change) | Answer a question with a changed version, which passes on and goes back to the asker, and print both outcomes. |
| [`decline`](#decline) | Decline a question, then give the asker the comment, and say whether the comment crossed. |
| [`cancel`](#cancel) | Cancel, as its asker, a question of the key's own, and print the outcome. |
| [`result`](#result) | Print how a question the key asked closed, its release, and the answer or version it fetched, as `give --wait` does. |
| [`get`](#get) | Fetch the next delivery queued for the key, or every one with `--all`, and print its body or the file it was written to. |
| [`mediators`](#mediators) | Print the labels config's entries, one JSON object per line, in the order the file lists them. |
| [`mcp`](#mcp) | Serve the mediators of the labels given to an agent as MCP tools, on standard input and output, as one party's client. |
| [`verify`](#verify) | Check a journal's receipts for validity under the mediator's key and, with a founding set, for conformance to the Accord, and print what was checked and what is not claimed. |
| [`show`](#show) | Decode one receipt without verifying it, and print what it says and what it claims. |
| [`log`](#log) | Export a verified journal as a log, one row per question, and with `--all` one for every crossing. |
| [`reconcile`](#reconcile) | Reconcile a journal's receipts with what each state directory kept, and print what was removed, unrecorded or missing. |
| [`released`](#released) | Say whether a file, a value inside it, or a part the key kept, is a part that crossed to the state directory's key, and under which receipt. |
| [`version`](#version) | Print which build the binary is: its version, commit, Go release and decision module. |

## `init`

Found an example Accord for one person, who holds every key, and print what to run next.

Usage: `placket init <example> [--dir <dir>] [--label <label>]`

| Argument | Values | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `<example>` | `approve`, `merge`, `handoff` | The entry point to set up: approve before apply, the out-gate of a merge, or an agent handoff. |

| Flag | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dir <dir>` | no |  | The directory to write the example in, empty or new; by default `<placket config dir>/<label>/`. |
| `--label <label>` | no |  | The label the example's entries of the labels config start with; by default the example's name. |
| `--json` | no |  | Print the result as one JSON object on standard output. |

Its `--json` object follows [commands-1](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-1-one-object-on-standard-output).

Exit codes: `0`, `3`.

## `bind`

Sign, as a principal, a binding that gives an actor its roles under one mediator and one policy until a time, and print it.

Usage: `placket bind --key <file> --actor <actor> --mediator <actor> --until <time> --role <role>... --policy <file>`

| Flag | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--key <file>` | yes |  | The principal's key file, which signs the binding. |
| `--actor <actor>` | yes |  | The actor reference the binding is for, as `key ref` prints it. |
| `--mediator <actor>` | yes |  | The mediator's actor reference, which the binding names. |
| `--until <time>` | yes |  | When the binding ends: a timestamp in whole seconds, such as 2099-01-01T00:00:00Z. |
| `--role <role>` | yes |  | A role the binding gives, such as `decider`; given once per role. |
| `--policy <file>` | yes |  | The founding set's policy, whose typed hash the binding names. |
| `--json` | no |  | Print the result as one JSON object on standard output. |

Its `--json` object follows [commands-1](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-1-one-object-on-standard-output), [commands-3](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-3-what-a-command-makes-or-fetches).

Exit codes: `0`, `3`.

## `founding`

Put a policy, a mediator, a card, the seals and the bindings in one founding set, check that it founds, and print it with its Accord id and card hash.

Usage: `placket founding --policy <file> --mediator <file> --card <file> --seal <file>... --binding <file>...`

| Flag | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--policy <file>` | yes |  | The policy: which roles each principal may grant. |
| `--mediator <file>` | yes |  | A file holding the mediator: its actor reference, its operator and how it runs. |
| `--card <file>` | yes |  | The card, as `card` prints it. |
| `--seal <file>` | yes |  | A declaration's seal entry, as `seal` prints it; given once per party. |
| `--binding <file>` | yes |  | A binding, as `bind` prints it; given once per binding. |
| `--json` | no |  | Print the result as one JSON object on standard output. |

Its `--json` object follows [commands-1](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-1-one-object-on-standard-output), [commands-3](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-3-what-a-command-makes-or-fetches).

Exit codes: `0`, `3`.

## `card`

Print this build's card, with the judges' configs given, and its card hash and the module it names.

Usage: `placket card --default [--judge <file>]...`

|---|---|---|---|

## `window`

Run the mediator of an Accord behind its door, on a unix socket, with its journal, until it is interrupted.

Usage: `placket window --key <file> --founding <file> --openings <dir> [--acceptances <file>] [--socket <path>] [--journal <dir>] [--judge <file>]...`

Its subcommands: [`window close`](#window-close).

| Flag | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--key <file>` | yes |  | The mediator's key file. |
| `--founding <file>` | yes |  | The founding set, as `founding` prints it. |
| `--openings <dir>` | yes |  | The directory of every member's opening, each as `seal` writes it. |
| `--socket <path>` | no |  | The socket to listen on; by default the Accord's own under the runtime directory. |
| `--journal <dir>` | no |  | The journal's directory; by default the Accord's own under placket's state directory. |
| `--acceptances <file>` | no |  | The members' acceptances; by default the `acceptances.json` beside the founding set, which the window writes once every member has accepted. |
| `--judge <file>` | no |  | A judge's config the card lists, given once per judge; a window needs exactly the card's. |
| `--json` | no |  | Print the result as one JSON object on standard output. |

Its `--json` object follows [commands-1](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-1-one-object-on-standard-output), [commands-3](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-3-what-a-command-makes-or-fetches).

Exit codes: `0`, `3`.

## `window close`

Close the Accord of a stopped window's journal: close each open question, write the close receipt last, and with `--socket` serve the closed Accord.

Usage: `placket window close --key <file> --founding <file> --journal <dir> --accord <id> [--acceptances <file>] [--openings <dir>] [--socket <path>]`

| Flag | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--key <file>` | yes |  | The mediator's key file. |
| `--founding <file>` | yes |  | The founding set of the Accord to close. |
| `--journal <dir>` | yes |  | The journal to close, of a window that is stopped. |
| `--accord <id>` | yes |  | The founding set's Accord id, given as a guard, since a close cannot be undone. |
| `--socket <path>` | no |  | Serve the closed Accord on this socket until interrupted; without it, the command exits once the close is written. |
| `--openings <dir>` | no |  | The directory of the members' openings; a close decides nothing, so it needs none. |
| `--acceptances <file>` | no |  | The members' acceptances, as `window` takes them. |
| `--json` | no |  | Print the result as one JSON object on standard output. |

Its `--json` object follows [commands-1](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-1-one-object-on-standard-output), [commands-3](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-3-what-a-command-makes-or-fetches).

Exit codes: `0`, `3`.

## `view`

Ask the window for the key's own view of a proposed Accord, keep it in the state directory, and print it.

Usage: `placket view <socket flags>`

| Flag | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--key <file>` | unless `--label` |  | The key file of the member the command speaks for; needed unless `--label` is given. |
| `--socket <path>` | unless `--label` |  | The window's socket; needed unless `--label` is given. |
| `--accord <id>` | unless `--label` |  | The Accord id the window serves; needed unless `--label` is given. |
| `--label <label>` | no |  | A mediator of the labels config, by its label, or by its Accord id when it has none, in place of `--key`, `--socket` and `--accord`. |
| `--state <dir>` | no |  | The member's state directory; by default `<key file>.state/<the Accord id's hex>/`. |
| `--json` | no |  | Print the result as one JSON object on standard output. |

Its `--json` object follows [commands-1](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-1-one-object-on-standard-output), [commands-3](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-3-what-a-command-makes-or-fetches).

Exit codes: `0`, `2`, `3`.

## `give`

Give another member one part, and print the outcome: pass, block, or ask, with the question's id.

Usage: `placket give <socket flags> --to <actor> --kind <kind> (--text <text> | --file <file> [--as <form>]) [--re <id>] [--topic <topic>] [--keep] [--wait]`

| Flag | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--key <file>` | unless `--label` |  | The key file of the member the command speaks for; needed unless `--label` is given. |
| `--socket <path>` | unless `--label` |  | The window's socket; needed unless `--label` is given. |
| `--accord <id>` | unless `--label` |  | The Accord id the window serves; needed unless `--label` is given. |
| `--label <label>` | no |  | A mediator of the labels config, by its label, or by its Accord id when it has none, in place of `--key`, `--socket` and `--accord`. |
| `--state <dir>` | no |  | The member's state directory; by default `<key file>.state/<the Accord id's hex>/`. |
| `--to <actor>` | yes |  | The receiver: a member's actor reference. |
| `--kind <kind>` | yes |  | The part's kind, which the terms select on. |
| `--text <text>` | no |  | The body, as text; one of `--text` and `--file` is needed. |
| `--file <file>` | no |  | A file holding the body, read as `--as` says. |
| `--as <form>` | no | `text` | How `--file` is read: `text`, `raw` or `data`, data being one JSON value in canonical form. |
| `--re <id>` | no |  | What the part is about, such as a question's id. |
| `--topic <topic>` | no |  | The part's topic. |
| `--keep` | no |  | Keep the part given in the state directory's `kept.jsonl`. |
| `--wait` | no |  | When the part is asked about, wait until its question closes, holding no lock, and print what `result` prints. |
| `--json` | no |  | Print the result as one JSON object on standard output. |

Its `--json` object follows [commands-1](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-1-one-object-on-standard-output), [commands-2](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-2-outcomes-questions-and-answers).

Exit codes: `0`, `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`.

| Flag | Required | Default | What it is |

| `--label <label>` | no |  | A mediator of the labels config, by its label, or by its Accord id when it has none, in place of `--key`, `--socket` and `--accord`. |
| `--state <dir>` | no |  | The member's state directory; by default `<key file>.state/<the Accord id's hex>/`. |
| `--question <id>` | yes |  | The question's id: the receipt id of its ask. |
| `--text <text>` | no | `accepted` | The answer's text. |
| `--no-release` | no |  | Accept with no release: the part does not pass on. |

## `change`

Answer a question with a changed version, which passes on and goes back to the asker, and print both outcomes.

Usage: `placket change <socket flags> --question <id> (--text <text> | --file <file>) [--comment <text>] [--keep] [--no-release]`

| Flag | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--key <file>` | unless `--label` |  | The key file of the member the command speaks for; needed unless `--label` is given. |
| `--socket <path>` | unless `--label` |  | The window's socket; needed unless `--label` is given. |
| `--accord <id>` | unless `--label` |  | The Accord id the window serves; needed unless `--label` is given. |
| `--label <label>` | no |  | A mediator of the labels config, by its label, or by its Accord id when it has none, in place of `--key`, `--socket` and `--accord`. |
| `--state <dir>` | no |  | The member's state directory; by default `<key file>.state/<the Accord id's hex>/`. |
| `--question <id>` | yes |  | The question's id: the receipt id of its ask. |
| `--text <text>` | no |  | The version, as text; one of `--text` and `--file` is needed. |
| `--file <file>` | no |  | A file holding the version, as UTF-8 text. |
| `--comment <text>` | no |  | A comment given to the asker after the change. |
| `--keep` | no |  | Keep the answer call signed, the salt minted and the version in `kept.jsonl`. |
| `--no-release` | no |  | Change with no release: the version goes back to the asker alone. |
| `--json` | no |  | Print the result as one JSON object on standard output. |

Its `--json` object follows [commands-1](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-1-one-object-on-standard-output), [commands-2](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-2-outcomes-questions-and-answers).

Exit codes: `0`, `1`, `2`, `3`.

## `decline`

Decline a question, then give the asker the comment, and say whether the comment crossed.

Usage: `placket decline <socket flags> --question <id> --comment <text>`

| Flag | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--key <file>` | unless `--label` |  | The key file of the member the command speaks for; needed unless `--label` is given. |
| `--socket <path>` | unless `--label` |  | The window's socket; needed unless `--label` is given. |
| `--accord <id>` | unless `--label` |  | The Accord id the window serves; needed unless `--label` is given. |
| `--label <label>` | no |  | A mediator of the labels config, by its label, or by its Accord id when it has none, in place of `--key`, `--socket` and `--accord`. |
| `--state <dir>` | no |  | The member's state directory; by default `<key file>.state/<the Accord id's hex>/`. |
| `--question <id>` | yes |  | The question's id: the receipt id of its ask. |
| `--comment <text>` | yes |  | The comment a decline needs: why, for the asker. |
| `--json` | no |  | Print the result as one JSON object on standard output. |

Its `--json` object follows [commands-1](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-1-one-object-on-standard-output), [commands-2](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-2-outcomes-questions-and-answers).

Exit codes: `0`, `1`, `2`, `3`.

## `get`

Fetch the next delivery queued for the key, or every one with `--all`, and print its body or the file it was written to.

| `--socket <path>` | unless `--label` |  | The window's socket; needed unless `--label` is given. |
| `--accord <id>` | unless `--label` |  | The Accord id the window serves; needed unless `--label` is given. |
| `--label <label>` | no |  | A mediator of the labels config, by its label, or by its Accord id when it has none, in place of `--key`, `--socket` and `--accord`. |
| `--state <dir>` | no |  | The member's state directory; by default `<key file>.state/<the Accord id's hex>/`. |
| `--out <dir>` | no |  | Write each body to a file of this directory, and print its path in place of the body. |
| `--keep` | no |  | Keep each delivery in `kept.jsonl`. |
| `--all` | no |  | Fetch every delivery waiting, in order, under one state lock. |
| `--wait <seconds>` | no |  | Wait at most this many seconds, up to 60, holding no lock, until a delivery is queued. |
| `--json` | no |  | Print the result as one JSON object on standard output. |

Its `--json` object follows [commands-1](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-1-one-object-on-standard-output), [commands-3](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-3-what-a-command-makes-or-fetches).

Serve the mediators of the labels given to an agent as MCP tools, on standard input and output, as one party's client.

## `verify`

Check a journal's receipts for validity under the mediator's key and, with a founding set, for conformance to the Accord, and print what was checked and what is not claimed.

Usage: `placket verify --receipts <dir> (--mediator <actor> | --accord <id> --founding <file>) [--founding <file>] [--acceptances <file>] [--answers <file>] [--subset] [--delivery <file>] [--superseded-by <file>] [--open <file>]... [--view <file>]`

| Flag | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--receipts <dir>` | yes |  | The journal's directory, whose `receipts.jsonl` is checked. |
| `--mediator <actor>` | no |  | The mediator's actor reference, under which the receipts are checked; one of `--mediator` and `--accord` is needed. |
| `--accord <id>` | no |  | The Accord id, the one value given out of band: the mediator's reference comes from the founding set whose typed hash it is. |
| `--founding <file>` | no |  | The founding set, for conformance to the Accord; needed with `--accord`. |
| `--acceptances <file>` | no |  | The founding set's acceptances; by default the `acceptances.json` beside it. |
| `--answers <file>` | no |  | A file of answer calls, one a line, read beside the journal's `answers.jsonl` to witness answers. |
| `--subset` | no |  | The receipts are a subset, whose chains may start late; completeness is then not claimed. |
| `--delivery <file>` | no |  | A delivery, as `get --json` saved it, whose body and salt are checked against its receipt. |
| `--superseded-by <file>` | no |  | The founding set of the Accord that supersedes this one, whose supersedes must pin this journal's close; it needs `--accord` and `--founding`. |
| `--open <file>` | no |  | A member's opening, given once per opening, so its seal and its terms are checked. |
| `--view <file>` | no |  | One member's own view, as it kept it, to check that member's receipts against; it needs `--founding`. |
| `--json` | no |  | Print the result as one JSON object on standard output. |

Its `--json` object follows [commands-1](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-1-one-object-on-standard-output), [commands-4](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-4-claims-and-records), [commands-8](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-8-what-verify-prints).

Exit codes: `0`, `1`, `3`.

## `released`

Say whether a file, a value inside it, or a part the key kept, is a part that crossed to the state directory's key, and under which receipt.

Usage: `placket released --state <dir> [--file <file>] [--kind <kind>]... [--at <pointer> (--value-file <file> | --value <text>)] [--re <id>] [--from <actor>] [--every]`

| Flag | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--state <dir>` | yes |  | The state directory of the key the part crossed to. |
| `--file <file>` | no |  | A file whose bytes are checked; without it, every part the key kept is tried. |
| `--at <pointer>` | no |  | A JSON Pointer into the body, where the value is checked; it needs one of `--value-file` and `--value`. |
| `--value-file <file>` | no |  | A file holding the value's bytes. |
| `--value <text>` | no |  | The value, as text. |
| `--re <id>` | no |  | Match only a kept part whose `re` is this; without `--file` only. |
| `--from <actor>` | no |  | Match only a receipt from this sender. |
| `--every` | no |  | Print every match, in fetch order, not only the first; without `--file` only. |
| `--kind <kind>` | no |  | Match only a receipt of this kind, given once per kind. |
| `--json` | no |  | Print the result as one JSON object on standard output. |

Its `--json` object follows [commands-1](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-1-one-object-on-standard-output), [commands-5](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-5-a-file-checked-against-what-crossed), [commands-6](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-6-a-value-checked-inside-what-crossed), [commands-7](../../spec/protocol.md#commands-7-everything-a-key-kept-checked-against-what-crossed).

Exit codes: `0`, `1`, `3`.

## Errors

Every code the command line prints, by where it comes from: its own codes under `adapters/cli`; the journal's under `adapters/journal`; a code in the window's reply by its member, `door`, `rejection` or `error`; and any other by the package that declares it. The same code under two keys has two sentences, each saying what it means there. `placket mcp`'s own codes are in the [mediator API's errors](mediator-api.md#errors).

Two kinds of code follow another and are not listed here. After `error verify`, the verifier's code is the protocol's ([verify-1](../../spec/protocol.md#verify-1-what-a-verifier-is-given)). After `error judge`, a judge config's code is the one `docs/adr/0023-judges.md` names. A founding code after `founding` is the protocol's too.

| From | Code | Cause and fix |
|---|---|---|
| `adapters/cli` | `body` | A give names no body or two; give exactly one of --text and --file. |
| `adapters/cli` | `card` | The card could not be built with the judges given; check each --judge file. |
| `adapters/cli` | `changed` | A change has no version, an empty one, or a file that is not UTF-8; give the version with --text or --file. |
| `adapters/cli` | `comment` | A decline has no comment, or a comment is not UTF-8; give a comment in UTF-8. |
| `adapters/cli` | `data` | A file given with --as data is not one JSON value in a form the canonical form takes; fix the file, or give it with --as raw. |
| `adapters/cli` | `delivery` | The --delivery file is not a delivery, or its receipt is none of the receipts; give a delivery of this journal, as get --json saved it. |
| `adapters/cli` | `dir-not-empty` | The directory init would write in holds something already, and init wrote nothing; give --dir an empty or new directory. |
| `adapters/cli` | `file` | A file or directory the command reads or writes could not be read or written, or is not a regular file, and the detail names which, or kept when a fetched body could not be written and was kept in kept.jsonl instead; check the path, and take a kept body from kept.jsonl. |
| `adapters/cli` | `format` | The log's --format is neither json nor csv, --words and --no-words were both given, or --json was given with --format csv; give one format, and --json only with json. |
| `adapters/cli` | `founding` | The founding set, an opening or the acceptances do not found the Accord, and the detail names the founding code, kernel for a card of another module than this build's, or judge for judge configs that are not the card's; fix the file the detail names, or run the build the card names. |
| `adapters/cli` | `internal` | The command failed in a way no other code names; run it again, and report it if it persists. |
| `adapters/cli` | `judge` | A --judge file is not a judge's config, and the detail names its code; fix the config as docs/adr/0023-judges.md says. |
| `adapters/cli` | `path` | The --at path is not a JSON Pointer; write it empty, or with a slash before each token. |
| `adapters/cli` | `seal` | The declaration is not one object signed by the key whose actor it names, or its opening could not be made; seal a declaration this key signed. |
| `adapters/cli` | `terms` | The terms are not one JSON object a declaration can carry, or could not be signed; fix the terms file. |
| `adapters/cli` | `text` | A text given on the command line, or a file read as text, is not UTF-8; give UTF-8, or give the file with --as raw. |
| `adapters/cli` | `until` | The binding's --until is not a timestamp in whole seconds; write it as 2099-01-01T00:00:00Z is written. |
| `adapters/cli` | `usage` | The command, an argument or a flag is not one it takes, a flag's value is not of its form, or a flag it needs is missing, as the line before says; run it as its usage in the CLI reference says. |
| `adapters/cli` | `verify` | The receipts do not verify, and the detail names the verifier's code with the file and the line, accord or card for a journal of more than one Accord or card, or superseded for a successor that does not pin this log's close; restore the journal, or give the successor that supersedes this Accord. |
| `adapters/client` | `asked` | What the window shows of the question is not the part its ask's receipt names, so nothing was signed; list the questions again. |
| `adapters/client` | `bad-config` | The labels config is not in its format; fix mediators.json against api/config/mediators.json. |
| `adapters/client` | `envelope` | The envelope could not be signed; check the key file holds a key. |
| `adapters/client` | `label-taken` | Two entries of the labels config have one label; give each entry its own label. |
| `adapters/client` | `mediator-collision` | Two entries of the labels config use one socket for two Accords, one state directory, or one Accord id with no label; give each its own socket, key or label. |
| `adapters/client` | `rand` | The source of randomness failed; call again. |
| `adapters/client` | `reply` | The window's reply is not what the call asked for; check the socket reaches this Accord's window. |
| `adapters/client` | `unknown-mediator` | No mediator served has that name; name one by its label, or by its Accord id when it has none, as mediators lists them. |
| `adapters/client` | `view` | The key keeps no view of this Accord to accept; run placket view first. |
| `adapters/journal` | `journal` | A file of the journal is not what a window wrote, or could not be read or written, and the detail names the file, its line and the core's code; restore the journal, or finish a cut close with placket window close. |
| `adapters/journal` | `journal-locked` | Another window holds the journal; stop that window, or give this one another journal. |
| `adapters/keyfile` | `key` | The key file does not hold a key; give the path of a key placket key new made. |
| `adapters/keyfile` | `key-exists` | A file is already at the key's path; choose another path. |
| `adapters/keyfile` | `key-mode` | The key file can be read by others; make it mode 0600. |
| `adapters/keyfile` | `key-read` | The key file could not be read; check its path and its owner. |
| `adapters/keyfile` | `key-write` | The key file could not be written; check the directory. |
| `adapters/local` | `cursor` | The window could not draw its cursors' key; start it again. |
| `adapters/local` | `judge` | The window's judge configs are not the ones its card lists; start it with the card's judges. |
| `adapters/local` | `reply` | What the window sent is not a reply; check the socket is a placket window's. |
| `adapters/local` | `socket` | The window could not be reached, or went away before it replied; start the window, or check the socket path. |
| `adapters/local` | `socket-path` | The socket path is longer than the system takes; use a shorter one. |
| `adapters/state` | `state` | A file of the state directory could not be read or written, or is not in its format; check the directory and its files. |
| `adapters/state` | `state-actor` | The state directory belongs to another key; give each key its own state directory. |
| `door` | `bad-call` | The call is not in the door's format, or its wait is not a whole number from 0 to 60; check the call against the mediator API. |
| `door` | `bad-signature` | The call's signature does not verify under its caller's key; sign it with the key it names. |
| `door` | `door-internal` | The window failed after the call passed its checks; call again, and see the window's log if it fails again. |
| `door` | `judge-busy` | The caller's last give is still with a judge; wait for its reply, then give again. |
| `door` | `not-founded` | The Accord is proposed, not founded: every member must view and accept its view first; run placket view and placket accept. |
| `door` | `replayed` | The window has seen the call's nonce already; call again with a fresh nonce. |
| `door` | `stale` | The call's time is more than 60 seconds from the window's clock; set the clock right and call again. |
| `door` | `too-large` | The call is longer than the door reads; send a smaller part. |
| `door` | `wrong-accord` | The window serves another Accord than the call names; check the mediator's Accord id. |
| `error` | `action` | No mediator returns this code any more; update the window. |
| `error` | `answer` | No mediator returns this code any more; update the window. |
| `error` | `at` | A time does not keep the timestamp rule; the window's clock is wrong, so check it. |
| `error` | `close` | The journal was cut inside a close; run placket window close to finish it. |
| `error` | `closed` | The Accord is closed already; nothing more can close it. |
| `error` | `held` | A reloaded delivery is queued by no receipt; restore the journal's held files. |
| `error` | `internal` | The mediator could not write a receipt or delivery; see the window's log and restart it. |
| `error` | `journal` | A reloaded receipt does not verify or names another Accord; restore the journal or close the Accord. |
| `error` | `question` | A reloaded open question does not match the receipts; restore the journal's questions file. |
| `error` | `salt` | No mediator returns this code any more; update the window. |
| `error` | `unfounded` | The window's mediator is not founded; restart the window on its founding set. |
| `rejection` | `accord-mismatch` | The message names another Accord than the window's; name this mediator's Accord. |
| `rejection` | `answer-body` | The answer's text and salt do not fit its call; send the text whose salted digest the call signs. |
| `rejection` | `answer-call` | The answer call does not read, names another Accord, or is not the caller's; sign it with the answering key for this Accord. |
| `rejection` | `closed` | The Accord is closed and takes no give or answer; found its successor and use that. |
| `rejection` | `envelope-hash` | The envelope names another message than the one sent; sign the envelope over this message's hash. |
| `rejection` | `envelope-sequence` | The envelope's seq is not above the last the mediator took from this key; give at the next seq. |
| `rejection` | `envelope-signature` | The envelope's signature does not verify under the giver's key; sign it with the giving key. |
| `rejection` | `extension-missing` | The message lacks placket's extension or its role; build it as a member gives one. |
| `rejection` | `no-open-question` | No question of that id is open; list the open questions, or ask for the result. |
| `rejection` | `not-a-member` | The key is not a member of the Accord; use a key the founding set binds. |
| `rejection` | `not-an-answerer` | The key may not answer or cancel that question; only its answerers answer it, and only its asker cancels it, while it has answerers. |
| `rejection` | `not-canonical` | The message is not in canonical form; send its canonical bytes. |
| `rejection` | `one-body` | The part must carry exactly one body, a text, a raw body or data; send one. |
| `rejection` | `one-part` | The message must carry exactly one part; send each part on its own. |
| `rejection` | `part-metadata` | The part's kind or salt is missing or malformed; give a kind and a salt of 32 bytes. |
| `rejection` | `receiver-unknown` | The receiver is not a member of the Accord; give to a member's actor reference. |
| `rejection` | `url-unsupported` | A part given by URL does not cross; send its body. |
